items.title: US consumers are extremely bullish on stocks: The perceived probability among US consumers that US stock prices will be higher 1-year from now increased +0.5 percentage points in July, to 41.4%, the highest since April 2021. Since March, this percentage has risen +5.1 points, marking the 2nd-highest reading since the 2020 pandemic. By comparison, the April 2020 peak was 51.8%. By age, consumers under 40 are the most optimistic, at 42.0%, the 2nd-highest since September 2024. This is followed by the 40-59 age group, at 41.5%, the highest since January 2025, and consumers over 59, at 41.1%, the highest since September 2025. Bullish sentiment is spreading across all consumer age groups.

The US job market is losing workers at an alarming pace:

The US labor force participation rate fell -0.1 percentage point in July, to 61.4%, the lowest since May 2020.

This metric measures the proportion of working-age Americans either employed or actively looking for work.

items.content:
Tech sector breadth is rapidly improving:

75% of S&P 500 technology sector stocks finished above their 200-day moving average last week, the highest percentage since October 2024.

This marked the first time in 219 trading days that this threshold was reached, ending the 9th-longest streak on record.

By comparison, the longest stretch during which fewer than 75% of tech stocks traded above their 200-day moving average lasted 759 trading days, ending on April 22, 2003, following the Dot-Com Bubble burst.

Historically, each time such a streak ended, the technology sector returned +2.5% on average over the following month and +7.3% over the next 3 months.

After 6 months and 12 months, the average gains were +15.5% and +33.4%, respectively.

Meanwhile, 69% of Nasdaq 100 stocks are now trading above their 200-day moving average, near the highest percentage since July 2025.

The tech stock rally is gaining momentum.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Aug 13, 2026
